key_insight: This paper introduces Bi-CFM, a bidirectional generative framework that can infer likely initial conditions from a chaotic system’s final state. It tackles the inherent uncertainty of chaos by learning distribution-to-distribution mappings rather than a single deterministic reverse path.
problem_solved: It addresses inverse problems in chaotic dynamics: recovering initial states from observed final states despite ill-posedness, non-uniqueness, instability, and the difficulty of time-reversing chaotic evolution.
method: Uses Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching (Bi-CFM) to learn both forward and backward mappings between initial-state and final-state distributions.
Models the stochastic nature of chaotic trajectories, allowing multiple plausible initial conditions rather than forcing one exact inverse.
Conditions the flow on observed states to generate reverse estimates that are consistent with the system’s chaotic dynamics.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a principled way to solve inverse problems where standard regression fails due to ambiguity and instability. It is especially useful for scientific ML settings involving chaotic simulators, state estimation, and reconstruction from sparse observations.
visual_elements: A two-way arrow diagram showing initial states mapping to final states and back via Bi-CFM.
A chaotic trajectory plot illustrating forward evolution and uncertain reverse reconstruction.
A distribution comparison graphic showing single-point prediction versus multi-modal inverse solutions.
An icon-based pipeline: observe final state -> condition on it -> generate candidate initial states -> validate against dynamics.
paper_title: Solving Inverse Problems of Chaotic Systems with Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching
paper_authors: Peiyan Hu, Jian Zhang, Jiashu Pan, Ruiqi Feng, Tao Zhang
